claim: With an orientation scan corrected for trials and a null drawn with the same exposure, a cubic-axis alignment statistic keeps its false-alarm rate at or below 5% on isotropic skies, on a 6.5% dipole and on non-uniform exposure, while detecting a 10% axis-aligned fraction at n = 2000 events with power >= 0.5; without the exposure correction, non-uniform exposure alone triggers it (> 5%).
name: lattice_anisotropy
reason: uncorrected exposure triggered at only 0 of 5 seeds: the required negative case tested nothing
refute_if: false alarm > 0.05 on the dipole OR on exposure-corrected skies, OR power < 0.5 at n=2000 & f=0.10 - any at >=3 of 5 seeds; INCONCLUSIVE if uncorrected exposure does NOT exceed 0.05 false alarm at >=4 of 5 seeds (the negative case then tested nothing)
